concepts.anchor: replace the two stale paragraphs under ## Role-based access control beginning `Metronome documents three built-in roles` and `New API tokens`
concepts.proposed_markdown:
Metronome documents three out-of-the-box display roles: Administrator has full CRUD access to all Metronome components; Writer has CRUD access except API-key creation and administrative settings such as data-export setup; and Reader can view all components but cannot create, update, or delete. With SSO, the customer's identity provider maps users through a customer-named claim (`role` is recommended) whose documented values are `admin`, `writer`, `reader`, or a custom role created with the Metronome team. A missing role is denied by default, although the customer can submit another default through the support portal; without SSO, users who have Metronome access receive full permissions. Custom roles are supported, but this page does not define their permission units or design lifecycle.

New API tokens can be assigned Administrator, Writer, or Reader at creation under **Developer > API tokens**; the token inherits the selected role's permissions, and the assigned role cannot later be changed. A custom role must first be created through the support portal. The authentication reference separately says tokens inherit the creating user's permissions by default and can be restricted by access level, environment, or endpoint through support. The sources do not define precedence or whether support-mediated scope changes affect an assigned immutable role, and the RBAC guide does not define enforcement or propagation timing. [[source-metronome-guides-platform-configuration-role-based-access-rbac]]
warnings: Replace the stale `admin, member, and viewer` display-role wording; preserve Administrator, Writer, and Reader as display names and `admin`, `writer`, and `reader` as claim values.
Do not infer precedence between token role selection and default permission inheritance, or enforcement and propagation behavior for role or scope changes.
